info.title: EDUNEXUS API
info.description: **0.111.9 quiets every form and removes one box on Academic history, and changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration. A field hint explains rather than records, so it now follows the workspace one notes switch like every other description, off by default: a form opens as its labels and its boxes, and the explanation is one click above it. A rejection is not a note and is never folded with them. The General average box is gone from Add a school year, asked for - but a year that already carries one keeps it, because the SF10 prints a General Average row per block and a correction sending null would have wiped a figure off an official form; what this removes is typing a new one, not the record (2026-11-10).** **0.111.8 makes the offer to list a grade learning areas always visible on Academic history, and changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration. It rendered only when it had something to add, so on opening Add a school year - where the grade still reads Choose - there was nothing at all, and it was reported twice as a feature that had never been built. The line is now always present and names which of three states it is in: choose a grade and these can be listed, here is the button for that grade, or every area is already listed. All three are tested (2026-11-10).** **0.111.7 merges the 2026-11-10 interface work that was built on an older branch, and changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration. Seven changes. Two cards left the monthly consolidation screen - Membership and marks, whose reads write a record_access_events row naming every enrolment returned, and Transition history, which restated the status the page already badges; both endpoints still answer and are simply uncalled. The school attendance rule is chosen from stacked lines rather than a select, since its options are sentences that say what each reading does to the SF2, so Editor gained a radios field type that starts on nothing because that rule has no default. Grade offerings shows Include retired only where something at that grade is retired. Every titled note folds from its own heading and starts open, per note rather than under one shared preference, so quietening one card never hides a refusal on a screen nobody has opened; this supersedes the sheet-notes fold of 0.111.3 for callouts, which the school asked to be open by default. A class-list file instructions are drawn rather than written out, with the header still passed in from ROSTER_HEADER. The staff sign-in panel drops its footer link to the page it already frames, while the Staff portal control that falls back to that page stays. And List the learning areas on Academic history works where it is aimed: the control sat inside the sentence describing it, whose second line painted over its lower half and took the clicks, and the behaviour it was blamed for now has two tests (2026-11-10).** **0.111.6** changes no endpoint: the Overview says who is signed in. **0.111.5** changes no endpoint: the front page’s inner tabs open on a plain title. **0.111.4** changes no endpoint: the Grade offerings filters line up. **0.111.3** changes no endpoint: a sheet’s long notes fold behind the description switch. **0.111.2** changes no endpoint: Create sections takes names one at a time. **0.111.1** changes no endpoint: a rejected form says each problem once. **0.111.0** changes no endpoint, schema, permission or migration: a notification opens its source, and Promotion has no Subject averages tab. **0.110.0 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: three interface asks of 2026-11-09, built one at a time. The public front page inner tabs carried an empty dark panel above the heading, because .valley, the SVG backdrop those pages share, had no positioning rule at all and laid out inline at the SVG own size; it now carries the same position/inset/z-index that the home page illustration has always had, and the bottom padding that was holding a gap for it comes down. The password toggle keeps one name: aria-label was swapping while aria-pressed already carried the state, so the control said the same thing twice and a screen reader read it twice. And a screen description is folded away until asked for, behind a control that says what it will show, remembered in sessionStorage for the tab rather than the machine. **A refused sign-in still does not say whether the email or the password was wrong**, which was asked for and is recorded as a decision in docs/constraints.md: naming the wrong half tells anyone who can reach the page which addresses are staff accounts, and Supabase answers both with one invalid_credentials anyway, so telling them apart needs the service-role key in the runtime, which is an open gate. What was built is the actionable part - the refusal names both possibilities, says capitals and a trailing space count, and points at the recovery link, and the states that give nothing away about anybody else are told apart (2026-11-09).** **0.109.1 (migration 0072) narrows automatic enrolment to a promotion. 0069 carried three approved outcomes into the following school year: promoted and conditionally promoted at the next grade, and retained at the same grade. The school narrowed it the same day - automatic enrolment is for a learner recommended for promotion and then approved by the principal or administrative officer - so a retention no longer enrols anybody. Both halves of that sentence still hold for the ones that do: advance_approved_enrollment reads promotion_decisions, which only record_promotion_recommendations writes and only decide_promotions approves, so no automatic enrolment can skip either step. conditionally_promoted still counts as a promotion, because every other place in the schema already treats it as one - commit_next_year_placement adds a grade for it and the SF9 and SF10 certify the next grade for it. A retained learner loses nothing: the outcome is still recorded and approved, their enrolment, grades and SF9 are untouched, and promotionsDecide now answers why: retained for each of them instead of counting them among those waiting for next year, which the approval sheet reads back so nobody has to notice the absence later. They are enrolled for next year by the office, by their adviser pull, or by Next year classes, which still carries a retention deliberately because it is a reviewed preview a manager commits rather than a side effect of an approval (2026-11-09).** **0.109.0 (migration 0071) answers an SF9 question whose answer was mostly already yes. The school asked that an issued SF9 be preserved against the learner, school year and grade level, that a promoted learner start the next grade with a blank card, and that neither overwrite the other. Four of the five requirements were already structural and are now asserted rather than assumed: read_sf9_source takes an enrollment, every report-card record hangs off enrollment_id, a promotion creates a new enrollment with no records (0069), and form_issuances has a CHECK that an sf9 row names both an academic_year_id and an enrollment_id, with the prior a reissue looks for keyed on that same scope - so a Grade 2 issuance is a new row with supersedes_id null and can neither find nor overwrite a Grade 1 one, and no issuance row is ever updated or deleted. What did not exist is the history itself: nothing could say which of a learner years had an issued card, because an sf9 issuance has learner_id NULL so formIssuanceList learner_id filter matches none of them, and that table row policy shows a teacher only the forms they issued themselves. The new GET /api/v1/learners/{id}/sf9-history answers it, one row per school year: the grade, the class, whether that year card is issued, in progress, voided, or no_card for Kindergarten which prints none, and the serial and fingerprint of the issued one. It joins sections outward so a learner with no class yet still appears, decides every row with can_read_enrollment so no read scope widens, reads no grade, and names no staff member - it says a card was issued, never by whom. Promotion learner profile school-years table carries it as a Report card column. Also fixed: the SF9 of a learner enrolled at a grade with no class yet, which is every promoted learner between the approval and their new adviser pull. Its source type claimed section_name was a string and got a null, so the card printed an empty section box; it is nullable now and the card own warnings say the learner is not in a class yet (2026-11-09).** **0.108.0 (migration 0070) makes three things true that the school asked for on 2026-11-09. A term accepts grades only once it has started: a trigger on report_grades, report_values and report_notes refuses a reporting period whose starts_on is after today in Manila, with P1908/PERIOD_NOT_STARTED, so finishing one term opens nothing and the next opens on its own configured date. A term already begun never closes, because the ECR figures arrive after it is over, and the subject average, the general average and the remarks name no term and are not gated. Promotion is closed until a class report cards are complete: the new GET /api/v1/sections/{id}/promotion-readiness counts what that grade card prints - every learning area in every configured term, each subject average and remark, and a general average - against its currently enrolled learners, and both promotion writers refuse with P2002/PROMOTION_NOT_OPEN while one is missing. It reads no grade and names no learner, so it writes no access row. Kindergarten prints no card and so waits for nothing, which keeps its outcome recordable as the credential presented for Grade 1, and a descriptively graded grade is judged on its term narratives instead. And an approved outcome now carries the learner into next school year by itself: decide_promotions enrols them in the same transaction, at the next grade for a promotion or conditional promotion and the same grade for a retention, with no section, through the same place_enrollment every other enrolment uses, and answers with advanced, waiting_for_next_year and a per-learner advance saying what happened or why it did not. When the following school year does not exist yet the outcome is recorded and the carry-forward runs the moment that year is created, from an after-insert trigger on academic_years. Nothing is deleted, this year records are untouched, and nobody is enrolled twice (2026-11-09).** **0.107.0** changes no endpoint, schema, permission or migration: Next year’s classes redrawn, and the test pass over the UI notes. **0.106.0** changes no endpoint, schema, permission or migration: the front page may frame `/app` for Staff portal, and `/app` may be framed by its own origin only. **0.105.0** (migration 0069): `GET /waiting/count` answers how many class lists, endorsed outcomes and staff name corrections wait on the caller — numbers only, zeros for a teacher, naming no record and writing no access row. **0.104.0**: `GET /learners` takes `section_id`, narrowing to learners in that class in the active school year, under the same row security as every other filter; no schema, permission or migration changed. **0.103.0 changes no endpoint, schema, permission or migration**: the UI notes of 8 November, U1 — one rule for every box, a list read again kept on screen, a still front page, and a reason written by the system when Subjects & offerings or Academic history adds a record. **0.102.2 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: a manager could not approve a list whose rows carry their own grades. Such a list records grade_level as null - no one grade is true of it - and the approval sheet went on sending that null. The API read a null as 0, Kindergarten, until 0.101.1 refused it; after that the sheet answered "expected number, received NaN" and no mixed list could be approved at all. The grade is omitted now and the rows decide. The same null also made five places call a mixed list Kindergarten, including the sentence saying what approving would do; they name several grades instead (2026-11-07).** **0.102.1 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: the grade picker is gone from the adviser class-list form. Every learner already carries their own grade - typed on Add learner, or in the template grade_level column - so a grade for the whole list was a second place to say the same thing. The submission now sends no grade_level at all, and a row that names none is said on its own line when the list is checked, beside the other row problems. The API is unchanged and still accepts a grade for the whole file, which the office import uses (2026-11-07).** **0.102.0 (migration 0068) lets an adviser submit a list at ANY grade. 0064 allowed a grade list only at a grade the submitter advised a class at; the school asked twice for that to go. It is safe to drop because a submission creates nothing - it is a CSV file with a reason attached, and no learner record, enrolment or registry row exists until a manager approves it through the reviewed import, which checks every row and is refused whole if one is wrong. The gate decided only who may ASK. A class list naming a section is still refused unless the submitter advises that section, because it names a class and a class belongs to its adviser; a grade is still checked for being 0 to 6. The adviser screen now offers all seven grades with Each row says its own as the default, and no longer stops an adviser who advises no class yet (2026-11-07).** **0.101.2 (migration 0067) finishes what 0065 started. Every function that answers which class a learner was in on a given day carries its own copy of the timeline resolution, and each ordered by effective_on alone and stopped at one - so two entries sharing a date tied and the earlier won. 0065 fixed two of them; seven were left. A learner the office registered and the adviser took in the same morning therefore showed on the Learner registry, which reads the enrolment row, and was missing from the SF2, the SF4 counts, the SF9, the absence monitor, the school-wide attendance summary, their own attendance record and the monthly guard - exactly the shape the school reported. Each is restated with the tie broken on array order, which resolve_enrollment_timeline already builds by enrollment_version. Nothing else in them changes, and nothing changes for an enrolment whose events fall on different days. A test now walks pg_proc itself and fails if any function still carries the untie-broken form, so the next reader cannot quietly reintroduce it (2026-11-07).** **0.101.1 fixes the two faults the school had been hitting, both of them encoding traps rather than logic. (1) SQLSTATE 22P02 adding a school year: write_learner_prior_year took the learning areas as a bare JS array, and node-postgres sends an array as a PostgreSQL ARRAY LITERAL, not JSON, so the cast to jsonb failed. Every other jsonb argument in the codebase was already stringified; this one was not. PGlite encodes an array and an object alike, which is why no test caught it and why it only ever failed against the real server. A guard in the database layer, applied by the real pool and the test harness alike, now refuses any parameter the driver would mis-encode - it immediately found a second one. (2) An adviser could not submit a list: grade_level null coerced to 0, which is Kindergarten, so the API refused a grade they do not advise. Null is now refused rather than read as a grade, and a grade of none is said by omitting the field. The academic history also asks for the start and end year separately, the end filled in as the start is typed and checked against it; only the start is kept, as an SF10 block has one year (2026-11-07).** **0.101.0 (migration 0066) names the person who acted on a notification, to the person it is addressed to. An adviser read "Not shown to you" in the Who column because actor_name came from a left join on edunexus.staff, whose staff_read policy is own-row-or-manager - the boundary answering rather than a gap, and recorded as such in 0.92.0. The school asked to see it. **staff_read is untouched**, which was the thing worth protecting: a teacher still cannot list staff, search them, or read any row but their own. notification_actor_name is a security-definer function taking a notification id and nothing else, answering only when that notification is addressed to the caller - so the one name it discloses is the one person who acted on your own inbox row, and it cannot be aimed at anybody else. Nothing is stored, so notifications already sent are named too; this is a read-side function rather than a new payload key, because that closed list exists to keep a learner out of a notification and is not widened for an unrelated reason (2026-11-07).** **0.100.2 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: four workspace fixes, two of which are screens still enforcing rules the database had already dropped. An adviser could not submit a second list while one waited - 0064 removed that index, and this screen went on refusing for two releases, so the database allowed it and the button did not. The bulk import required a grade to be chosen, which made the new template grade_level column unusable: it is optional now and stands only for the rows that leave theirs empty, with "Each row says its own" as the default. A half-typed class list survives a page refresh, kept in sessionStorage - the school lost a morning of typing to a reload - and is cleared on submit or with Start the list again; sessionStorage rather than localStorage because a draft holds learner names, birth dates and LRNs, so it dies with the tab like a session. Add one late learner is now Add learner (2026-11-07).** **0.100.1 (migration 0065) fixes two faults the school hit in use. (1) Add one late learner wrote a SEVEN-column header above nine-column rows, so the list was refused with "this row has 9 columns; the template has 7" - the header was wrong, not the rows. `TEMPLATE_HEADER` was a third copy of the column list frozen at 2026-10, and a fourth copy sat in the import hint; both are gone and a test now refuses any second spelling of the columns. (2) A learner registered and taken into a class on the SAME morning was missing from that day register and from the month the SF2 counts. Both readers resolved an enrolment timeline by ordering on `effective_on` alone and stopping at one, so two entries sharing a date tied and the earlier won - unreachable until 0062 allowed a same-day first class, which is what made it appear. The tie-break is the array order `resolve_enrollment_timeline` already builds by version. An unmapped database error now quotes its SQLSTATE, because the academic history refused with a bare message for three sessions and the cause could not be read off it (2026-11-07).** **0.100.0 (migration 0064) lets one class list hold several grades, and any number of lists wait. The template gains a ninth column, `grade_level`: 0 for Kindergarten then 1 to 6, with "Kinder" and "Grade 3" read too. A row's own grade wins, a row that leaves it empty takes the grade chosen for the file, and a row with neither is refused on its own line rather than taking the file down. `grade_level` on the import and the submission is therefore now OPTIONAL when the rows carry their own, and the receipt's grade is null for a mixed file. Each learner is enrolled at their own row's grade. Add one late learner gains the grade, and the address it had been silently dropping since it wrote only seven of the columns. The one-waiting-list-per-section and per-grade indexes are DROPPED: they made sense when a list was a grade, and what actually stops a learner being enrolled twice is unchanged - `place_enrollment` refuses a second enrolment in one school year. `submit_roster_grades` supersedes `submit_roster_list`, checking every grade a list holds against the grades the submitter advises a class at, so an adviser's reach has not widened by one learner. Files from both older templates still import (2026-11-07).** **0.99.0 (migration 0063) makes an adviser's individual registration reviewed like every other list, and tidies eight things the school asked for. `register_learner_into_section` has its grant withdrawn, not the function dropped, so 0054 and 0056 still describe something that exists and one line puts it back; a single learner is now a one-row class list the office approves. THE CONSEQUENCE TO KNOW: that was an adviser's only way to record a guardian, and the class-list template has no guardian columns, so a guardian is now a manager's field filled on the registry afterwards. A blank 500 on a database older than the code now answers 503 SCHEMA_BEHIND naming the migration command, because the bare "The request could not be completed." sent the school hunting through a file that was fine. Free text a person types is capitalised on save - names, school and section names, the source document and every reason - raising the first letter only and never lowering the rest. No endpoint, schema or error code changed beyond that: the rest is the workspace. Enrollment is renamed Admissions and loses "Enrol a learner"; the adviser's roster import derives its grade from the classes they advise and asks only when they advise two; offerings are chosen per grade and written to every class of it; and an SF10 scholastic block now sits in the panel for its grade, so a Grade 3 learner with no transcribed history shows two empty panels before theirs (2026-11-07).** **0.98.0 fixes three faults the school found in real use and adds the one capability they asked for with them (migration 0062). (1) An adviser could not take in a learner the office had registered THAT DAY: `move_enrollment` refuses a movement that does not advance the timeline, which is right between two classes and wrong for a first class, where the learner leaves nothing. Same day is now allowed when, and only when, the enrolment has no section; the future-date rule is untouched. (2) `POST /learners` inserted directly, so a manager could create a second record for one child whenever the LRN differed - the workspace warned and then let them continue, which is a warning and not a control. It now goes through `register_learner`, which applies the same name-and-birth-date guard an adviser has had since 0054, and a genuinely different child is registered with `distinct_reason`, written down and kept. (3) A class-list row that stopped one column short was refused as a broken file; a trailing empty cell is what Excel writes, so short rows are padded and the field rules decide what was actually missing. NEW: `POST /enrollments/:id/release` takes a learner back out of a class the caller advises, returning the enrolment to having no class - never to another class, never withdrawn, never touching the learner record. New codes P2605 and P2606 (2026-11-07).** **0.97.0 adds one shape to an existing module and no new endpoint: an adviser may submit a list at a GRADE, with no class. Migration 0061 makes `roster_submissions.section_id` nullable and adds `grade_level`, exactly one of the two per list; `submit_roster_list` replaces `submit_roster`, whose grant is withdrawn so there is one writer; and `decide_roster_submission` now matches a grade list against an import that landed its learners at that grade with no section, which is what 0048 already wrote. **The gate did not widen:** a grade list is allowed only at a grade the submitter advises a class at in that same year, raising P1701 otherwise - an adviser authority here comes from the sections they advise, so every learner they can put on a grade list they could already have put on their own class list. One list waits per section and one per grade of a year. Approved learners land on the registry in no class, and the advisers of that grade take in the ones who are theirs through the pull 0054 already built (2026-11-06).** **0.96.0 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: a manager now approves an adviser's class list on Enrollment, and the API it goes through is the one that was already there. The school ruled that Roster import stays the administrative officer's screen, which left the principal holding a notification about work they could not reach, so the approval moved to a screen both managers have. One **Approve and import** button makes the same three calls Roster import makes, in the same order - preview, commit, then the decision carrying that receipt - because `decide_roster_submission` accepts a list only with an import the approver themselves committed for its section (P1704). Both managers could always make all three: every one is manager-gated and the writer checks `is_manager()`. The screen sends no duplicate resolutions, so a row that may be a learner already on file stops the preview, writes nothing and leaves the list waiting; pointing a row at the learner it means stays on Roster import, because guessing it would make two records for one child (2026-11-06).** **0.95.5 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: it is a wording fix in the workspace. The notification *A class list is waiting to be imported* goes to the principal as well as the administrative officer, but Roster import is hidden from the principal's navigation, so the row named a screen they had no way into and stopped - a dead end the school reported. 0.95.4 opened the screen to both managers; the school ruled that the import stays the administrative officer's, so this release closes it again and fixes what was actually wrong. A notification kind may now carry wording for a reader the screen is shut to, and this one reads "The administrative officer imports it". None of this was ever a permission: `decide_roster_submission` checks `is_manager()` and would accept either manager, and only the route table changed, in either direction (2026-11-06).** **0.95.3 changes no endpoint, schema, permission, error code or migration: it is a workspace fix, and the backend was already correct. An adviser whose own class holds nobody was told that no learners are currently assigned to their sections, and nothing else - true of their class, silent about the learners waiting to be taken into it, and so read as "there is nobody". The empty table on the Learner registry now names what it is describing and offers **Add learner** from inside it. `read_pullable_learners` is untouched and already lists the learners registered into the active year at the grade of the class, **with no class yet**, which was verified end to end: the unplaced learners at the grade an adviser advises are offered, another grade is not, taking one in assigns the enrolment the office already holds without a second learner or enrolment record, and a second take-in is refused `LEARNER_IN_CLASS`. The read scope is unchanged - an adviser still reads only the classes they advise, and the pull is still scoped to a section they advise (2026-11-05).** **0.95.2 changes no endpoint, schema, permission or error code: it is a workspace fix. The Add learner sheet an adviser uses now refuses a school year the principal has not activated, or one that has not begun, rather than showing an empty list and then failing the take-in. The refusal comes from the API itself: giving a class to a learner the office has registered is a `move_enrollment`, which refuses a future-dated movement, while enrolling one who holds no enrolment is a `place_enrollment`, which has no such check — so the same first day was refused by one path and silently accepted by the other. The backend is untouched; the school builds its classes once the year is activated (decided 2026-11-06).** **0.95.1 changes no endpoint, schema, permission or error code. It adds one operator command, `npm run seed:demo-registry`, which seeds a demonstration registry — learner profiles, one class per grade, and the source school year to promote out of — and deliberately stops before the next school year, promotion, next-year placement and the adviser pull, which are the school's own to perform. Its rehearsal recorded two defects in existing code: carrying more than fifty learners into next year in one request is refused, because `nextYearCommit` writes two record ids per learner into `record_access_events`, whose CHECK caps a row at one hundred; and `nextYearPreview` writes one per learner, so it is refused above one hundred.** **0.95.0 adds migration 0058: notifications for the monthly consolidation, promotion outcomes and the instructional calendar. No endpoint, schema, permission or error code changed. The attendance three report that a month moved between desks and carry no attendance figure of any kind — the absence-alert gate is untouched. adviser_assigned and adviser_removed are still not emitted: a section’s adviser is set by plain SQL in the service with no security-definer writer to replace, and granting notify to edunexus_app was refused.** **0.94.0 adds migration 0057: notifications for enrollment and class assignment. No endpoint, schema, permission or error code changed. The emission is at the intent boundary rather than the row writer — `place_enrollment` is called in a loop by the reviewed import and by next year’s placement, so it emits nothing, and `finish_import` sends one notification carrying a count while `move_enrollment`, which is one movement per request, sends one per movement.** **0.93.0 changes the workspace only: a bell in the top bar carrying the unread count, and the notification centre behind it. No endpoint, schema, permission or error code changed.** **0.92.0 adds notifications (migration 0056): a personal inbox, with GET /notifications, GET /notifications/count, POST /notifications/read and POST /notifications/read-all. None is manager-only and none has a manager branch, because an inbox is personal: the row policy answers only rows addressed to the caller, so a principal reads their own and not the school’s. No notification names a learner — the payload admits a closed list of keys enforced by a check constraint — and the count endpoint names no record and writes no record_access_events row, so a bell may poll it. The API cannot send one: notify is never granted to edunexus_app, so only a security-definer writer inside the transaction that made the change can. The first emitters are the four roster-submission events. New error code P2700. Nothing here alerts, messages or notifies on attendance: that gate stays shut.** **0.91.1 changes the workspace only: the Learner registry shows one learner in three parts — profile, academic history, enrollment — reading the same learner record, with no endpoint, schema, permission or error code changed.** **0.91.0 adds migration 0055: two more of a person’s own interface settings — spacing, and a small text size — saved on staff_profiles the way 0043’s and 0047’s are, through the same save_my_profile. No permission changed.** **0.90.6 adds one optional query parameter, `entity_table` on GET /audit-events, and changes no permission: the audit stays manager-only. 0.90.1 to 0.90.5 change the workspace only: no endpoint, schema, permission or error code changed.** **An adviser builds their own class, and the office oversees the historical encoding** (migration 0054). GET /academic-years/{id}/encoding-progress counts, for every section of a year and for the learners in no class yet, how many learners have an encoded previous year, how many have the Grade 1 credential and how many have neither, with the adviser named — manager-only, reads no rating, names no learner and writes no access record, exactly as the grade-entry read does. GET /sections/{id}/pullable-learners lists the learners an adviser may take into a class they advise: those registered for its school year at its grade with no class yet, and, with a search of at least two characters, a learner with no enrolment this year at all. POST /sections/{id}/pulls takes one in — a class is given to the enrolment they already hold, or they are enrolled at the section’s grade if they hold none — through `move_enrollment` and `place_enrollment`, the same two writers the registry form and the roster import use, so no second learner record is ever created. POST /sections/{id}/learners registers a new learner straight into that class, refused when a learner with the same name and birth date is already on the registry (LEARNER_ALREADY_ON_REGISTRY), because an adviser cannot search the registry and two records for one child is the failure that matters most. Both writers were replaced to allow an adviser only this: into a section they advise, and only giving a class to an enrolment that has none. Taking a learner out of another adviser’s class, withdrawing and re-entering stay manager-only, as does every profile correction. A teacher still reads only the learners in the classes they advise; a manager still reads the whole school. The class-list import registers learners **with no class yet**: POST /roster-imports/preview and /{id}/commit take `section_id` as before, or an `academic_year_id` and `grade_level` with `section_id` null, which enrols every learner in the file at that grade with no section (`place_enrollment`, the writer `enrollmentCreate` already used for one learner). This is how a school puts its whole roll on the registry before classes are settled; assigning a class afterwards is a movement on that one enrolment, never a second enrolment, so a learner never holds two enrolments for one year. A section that contradicts a year or grade sent beside it is refused (SECTION_MISMATCH) rather than silently resolved, and the destination is part of the reviewed plan, so committing a preview against another grade or section answers PREVIEW_CHANGED. The preview answers `section: null` with `academic_year_id` and `grade_level`, and the receipt carries `section_id: null` and `grade_level`. Unplaced learners are reported on the SF4 as counts by grade and sex, naming nobody, and the SF4 cannot be issued while any remain (FORM_UNPLACED_LEARNERS). The learner registry holds one line of **address** beside the name, LRN, birth date and sex (migration 0053), on POST and PATCH /learners and in every learner response.
